notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session with the skill installed, against a writable copy of the fixture repo (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt with the skill NOT installed. Grade by reading the resulting repo state + plan artifact + transcript; never grade the author's own memory. The fixture's package.json scripts (scripts/type-check.js, lint.js, test.js) actually execute and actually exit non-zero when the feature is absent or wrong — the verification feedback loop is REAL, not theatrical. Plan files for each scenario are pre-seeded in the fixture at .opencode/plans/<slug>.md. Eval 1 + Eval 2 share feat-offline-queue.md (the approved happy-path plan, exact plan-format.md contract). Eval 2's prompt adds an adjacent extra the plan's Excluded list names — tests scope discipline under prompt pressure, not feature mechanics. Eval 3 is a mechanical plan-reality mismatch: feat-offline-queue-rename.md lists the new file at src/outbox/queue.ts against the project's src/lib/<feature>.ts convention (AGENTS.md); the agent must correct the path, proceed, and add a dated History entry explaining the deviation — not silently follow the wrong path or stop. Eval 4 is a contract-breaking mismatch: feat-offline-queue-broken.md criterion 3 asserts replay survives a full browser close via the registered service worker, verified by `npm run test` in tests/offline-resume.test.ts — but neither the service worker file nor tests/offline-resume.test.ts appears in Files to Modify, and the plan's Schema/Type Impacts says `None.`; the agent must classify this as contract-breaking (criterion untestable as written, references infrastructure the plan does not add), STOP, report to the user, and route back to the design stage — not invent a service worker or silently drop the criterion. Assertions tagged [fix-verified] encode defects found and fixed during the eval loop — they are the regression net; do not remove without re-running the full loop.

Model coverage: fresh subagents via the task tool — single tier in practice (Go-tier unless the harness varies). Cross-tier (Zen-tier) validation is deferred until the harness supports varying subagent model binding; this is a documented deferral, not a silent skip. Re-run on a Zen-tier model when the harness permits.

Eval 5 = red-first-then-green core (fixture tdd-redfirst/feat-session-score: 3 testable unit ACs + a manual AC4, no pre-existing tests/impl; agent authors one unit test per AC BEFORE any source edit, runs it, confirms red for the right reason naming the missing scoreSession behaviour, then implements, greens verification, then runs the new coverage-and-quality gate). FAIL if it proceeds to implement against a harness-defect red). Eval 7 = COVERAGE-GATE REBALANCE leg (CORE proof of Decision 3 — fixture tdd-rebalance/feat-audit-log-dedupe: the AC1 wording plausibly reads as pure array dedupe so a reasonable red-first guess picks UNIT, but the real impl necessarily touches the store+client seam; the layer detector in scripts/test.js objectively reds on a vacant wrong-layer unit test with a named WRONG-LAYER/vacant message; the agent's Step 8 rebalance must supersede it and reauthor at the integration layer driving the REAL store through the FAKED client, re-proving via break/restore against src/stores/audit-store.broken.js. FAIL if never notices OR treats the red-first guess as immutable). Eval 7 makes 'no plan-format.md schema change' safe to rely on — the rebalance demonstrably corrects a wrong red-first guess downstream, every time. Eval 8 = coverage-gate NO-GAP-FOUND leg (co-graded with eval 5 against tdd-redfirst: the scoreSession linear impl has no real gap and no rebalancing is needed; the agent must EXPLICITLY say 'none needed' on rebalance and 'no high-value gap found beyond the AC set' on expand — an explicit negative is the closure signal; FAIL if it skips the gate or manufactures a padding test). Eval 9 = coverage-gate REAL-GAP leg (fixture tdd-realgap/feat-clip-duration: ACs name only the two happy clamps; the impl honors the AGENTS RangeError-on-negative convention, revealing a real error-path branch the ACs didn't name; scripts/test.js objectively reds on the uncovered AC gap; the agent adds exactly ONE targeted test via writing-unit-tests 'untested behaviour' mode, proves break/restore, does NOT expand beyond the one gap; FAIL if it ignores the gap OR over-expands with padding). Eval 10 = manual-only AC handling (co-graded with eval 5: tdd-redfirst's plan carries manual AC4; the agent must NOTE the manual AC (not red-first-tested, not silently dropped) rather than forcing a synthetic automated test). Evals 5, 8, and 10 share the tdd-redfirst fixture + prompt and are co-graded from one agent run.
